## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at `b410b57b`, reassessing the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5803495476) after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5804226138).

**Verified:** both findings from the previous review are resolved, and the two findings from the [first review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5791310535) have not regressed. One new, low-impact gap remains: on an upgraded system, the new tmpfiles entry takes effect only at the next boot.

| Previous finding | Status at `b410b57b` |
|---|---|
| The ancestor watch does not wake when the flag directory is created | **Resolved.** The ancestor fallback is gone. The watcher watches only `/dev` and the flag's own directory, so the flag's creation and deletion arrive as ordinary file events that pass `--include`. With the real `inotifywait` in private directories, the flag showed up after 0.1s when the directory already existed. When the directory and flag were created during a back-off, it took 4.0s (created 1s in) and 1.0s (created 4s in), which matches the reply's ~4s. |
| Redirection order in `omarchy-toggle-camera` (optional cleanup) | **Resolved.** All three writes, including `drivers_probe`, now redirect stderr first. The failed-open message is no longer printed. The exit status is still 1, so `\|\| true` still applies. |

**Verified:** the PR's shell test passes at this head. Its new watched-directory and tmpfiles assertions each fail against a matching negative control: the `711ec34a` watcher, and this head without the tmpfiles file. The 5s back-off still holds with no fd or child growth, and the `--include` regex only became narrower.

### The tmpfiles entry is not applied on upgrade

[`etc/tmpfiles.d/omarchy-camera.conf`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/b410b57b1f67d6007ebee9623ae2d79e31994359/etc/tmpfiles.d/omarchy-camera.conf) ships to `/etc/tmpfiles.d/`, because the omarchy-settings package copies `etc/` wholesale, and systemd-tmpfiles applies it at boot. Nothing applies it at upgrade time:
- Arch's tmpfiles pacman hook triggers only on `usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/*.conf`.
- The package's `post_upgrade` does not run systemd-tmpfiles.
- The PR adds no migration.

```text
upgrade installs /etc/tmpfiles.d/omarchy-camera.conf, no reboot yet
  /var/lib/omarchy absent
    -> inotifywait cannot watch the flag directory and exits at setup
    -> watcher backs off 5s, rescans, retries
       (no /dev/video* wake-ups either, because the whole watch failed)
  ends at: next boot | first camera disable | a pacman transaction that fires the hook
```

**Impact:** only systems without `/var/lib/omarchy` are affected, and how many that is was not measured. Systems that ran migration `1788025225` already have it, because the migration writes a machine-wide marker under it; deferred provisioning and the optional Windows VM setup also create it. ISO installs made after that migration shipped mark migrations as done without running them, so they can lack it. On such a system, a user who enables the widget (off by default) before rebooting gets 5s polling with a full process-descriptor scan each cycle, and camera use or unplug shows up within about 5s rather than immediately. The effect is bounded, with no busy loop.

**Suggested change:** also create the directory at upgrade time, for example with a migration that runs `install -d -m 0755 /var/lib/omarchy` as root. Two alternatives need a change in omarchy-pkgs: ship the entry under `/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/` so the Arch hook applies it in the same transaction, or run `systemd-tmpfiles --create` for this file in `post_upgrade`. None of these was tested.

---

**Test scope:** Source review of `711ec34a..b410b57b` and of the inotify-tools, systemd tmpfiles, Arch systemd packaging, omarchy-pkgs packaging and bash sources involved. Isolated command-level runs: the PR's shell test with negative controls, a redirection probe, and the real watcher with the real `inotifywait` in private directories with a synthetic USB interface, one run per timing case. No live `/dev` or `/var/lib`, udev, USB switching, root toggle, pacman transaction, boot or real systemd-tmpfiles run, PipeWire or desktop GUI. Suggested changes were not tested.
